subject: Urgent: request queue saturation causing checkout timeouts - mitigation plan
messages:
From: Jamal Price <jamal.price@core-retail.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: elena.park@core-retail.com
Date: 2027-05-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Checkout timeouts + p99 spikes since 5/21 — urgent

Hi Sofia,

We're seeing large p99 latency spikes and occasional 504s on our checkout flows since late last night (starts ~23:30 PDT 5/21). Error rate jumped from 0.2% to ~3.8% and p99 from 420ms to 4.2s — this hit a live checkout and caused ~120 failed orders in the last 6 hours.

Sample traces: TRACE-CR-001, TRACE-CR-004, TRACE-CR-019 (attached in request_traces_20270522.json). It looks like requests queue up and some never make it through your inference pool (we're using your hosted/text-generation route, model rwd-2f-large). Our retries amplify the backlog.

This is high severity for us — can we get an immediate mitigation plan and an ETA? We're ready to open an executive call if needed.

Thanks,
Jamal Price
Head of Engineering, Core Retail
jamal.price@core-retail.com
+1 415-555-0123

Jamal — thanks for flagging and for the trace bundle. We're on it. Short answer: we can implement a short-lived mitigation within 1 hour and follow with a targeted canary. Longer answer below with owners and proposed steps.

Immediate (1 hour):
- Ramp down client-side retries (if possible) to avoid amplifying the queue. We can give you a temporary guidance snippet.
- Route a subset (10-20%) of traffic away from the currently overloaded pool (us-west-2-pool-A) to us-west-2-pool-B or an eu-west fallback for read-only requests.
- Increase your per-customer concurrency cap by 20% for 2 hours to allow in-flight requests to drain.

Engineering leads: Dylan Brooks (runtime) and Karthik Iyer (routing & capacity) are looped in. I'll coordinate the exec updates and procurement asks.

Attachments: I've attached a brief ops checklist and requested Dylan to add diagnostic notes.

Can you confirm whether the checkout requests are write-heavy (some custom reranking) or largely read/generation-only? That affects fallback routing.

I'll set up a short bridge for 10:00 PDT.

— Sofia

> On May 22, 2027, at 09:12, Jamal Price <jamal.price@core-retail.com> wrote:

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, Jamal Price <jamal.price@core-retail.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-22T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Checkout timeouts + p99 spikes since 5/21 — diagnostic notes and mitigations

Sofia / Jamal — I dug through the traces and infra metrics. TL;DR: queue saturation + KV cache churn causing long-tail latency. Details: 

What we saw
- us-west-2-pool-A experienced sustained token throughput near its configured soft limit between 23:15 and 03:40 PDT. Concurrency cap for Core Retail hit 95% of allowed (cap=120) and then request bursts led to large request queuing in the front-end router.
- KV cache eviction rates rose sharply due to bursty sequence-length increases on ~8% of requests (custom reranking in checkout). Misses led to extra GPU work and amplification of the p99.
- Backpressure propagated: front-end queued requests and then timeouts triggered retries from your client which made the tail worse.

Immediate mitigations we can apply now (implemented as emergency runbook):
1) Bump per-tenant concurrency cap: +20% (from 120 -> 144) for a rolling 2 hour window to allow backlog to clear.
2) Enable prefix KV caching on your model variant (less aggressive memory use but higher hit for checkout patterns).
3) Route 15% of checkout-only traffic to us-west-2-pool-B; route non-checkout (analytics/low-priority) to eu-west fallback.
4) Short-term token budget cap on rewrite/rerank calls (reduce max gen tokens to 256 for retry window).

Risks & notes:
- Increasing concurrency temporarily increases aggregate GPU utilization — acceptable as a short emergency window, but sustained higher caps require Dedicated capacity.
- KV prefix caching may change latencies for some sequences; we will monitor quality metrics and have an automated rollback if score delta > 1.5%.

Planned canary: 1 hour canary with 5% traffic, then 20% for one hour, then full roll. Will run health checks on p95/p99, error rate, and quality evals.

I've pushed a diagnostic summary (diagnostic_summary_20270522.pdf) and traces into the shared Drive.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
dylan_brooks@redwood.ai

Thanks Dylan and Sofia — appreciate the quick triage. Please proceed with the mitigations (bump cap + route + KV caching) and start the canary. We need clear runbook steps and an ETA for when we can expect p99 back near baseline.

Also we will need: 
- Formal incident timeline for our audit.
- Confirmation on whether this constitutes a breach of our SLA and what remediation (credits) Redwood will offer if uptime/latency targets were impacted. I'm CCing procurement to start the contract thread.

If this persists beyond the emergency window, Core Retail will evaluate Dedicated capacity options — we need guidance on sizing.

Jamal

Subject: Exec-level ask: temporary capacity uplift + discretionary credit for Core Retail

Team — following the emergency mitigations (applied 5/22) the canary completed and p99 returned to ~520ms within 90 minutes of the cap bump and routing changes. Core Retail is satisfied with the fix but has asked for two executive items:

1) Temporary capacity uplift: approve a 30% per-tenant concurrency uplift for 72 hours if we see another surge while they evaluate Dedicated sizing. Owner: Ops (Karthik) / Runtime (Dylan).
2) Discretionary credit: customer requests good-faith SLA remediation for the impacted window (est. 6 hours of degraded experience, request: one month of service credit). Owner: Sales (Sofia) — needs VP Sales + Legal approval.

Context: Core Retail is strategically important (retail checkout during peak season); public-facing outage risk. They are evaluating Dedicated capacity in parallel but want a safety valve in the meantime.

Requested approvals & next steps:
- Karthik: confirm feasibility and any constraints on short-term uplift and whether we need to spin up extra instances vs. adjusting caps.
- Dylan: confirm monitoring checks we will use to auto-revert uplift and canary config to minimize risk to other tenants. Attach proposed canary config (proposed_canary_config.yaml).
- Lauren (Sales Ops): estimate financial exposure for a one-month credit and advise approval route.
- VP Sales & Head of Ops: please reply with approval/next steps by EOD tomorrow 5/26.

Sofia Ivanova
